inter_arrival_shape.source: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce public dataset, within-day gaps
inter_arrival_shape.deployed_as: poisson operating point (arrival_mode: poisson); Olist bootstrap is the A2 replay

arrival_rate.note: Load is the independent variable of the study and is swept in the robustness grid; it is not a distributional claim.

sla_due_triangular.source: Olist purchase -> estimated delivery. AIC-best family is lognormal; value[] is a moment-matched triangular, not what config.yaml deploys (15, 45, 90).

processing_time_triangular.source: Three-point time standard for manual picker-to-parts order picking (travel + search + pick), after de Koster, Le-Duc & Roodbergen (2007) and the time-standard decomposition in Tompkins et al., Facilities Planning. Not fitted: the Olist trace carries no warehouse pick-time field, and its purchase-to-approval latency is not a pick time.

shelf_life_triangular.note: No public trace carries product expiry. Swept in the sensitivity analysis; the binding rate is measured by experiments/perishability_diagnostic.py.

perishable_prob.note: Olist food/drink share is 0.0099, a property of that marketplace's product mix rather than of a perishable-goods warehouse. Varied across scenarios.
